content.user_title: Review GitHub PRs With Multi-Agent Checks
content.value_statement: Pull request review can miss security, performance, test, and documentation issues. This skill coordinates specialized agents and formats actionable GitHub review feedback.
actual_capabilities: Initializes a mesh swarm for five specialized reviewer agents.
Defines parallel review tasks for security, performance, quality, tests, and documentation.
Fetches pull request context through a referenced GitHub API script.
Aggregates findings into a merge readiness report with weighted scoring.
Prepares GitHub review comments, labels, and inline feedback commands.
Includes a Graphviz diagram of the review workflow.
limitations: Referenced scripts and review criteria files are not included in the scanned package.
Requires GitHub permissions and compatible MCP or Claude Flow tools.
Command examples should be reviewed before execution in untrusted repositories.
It does not replace human approval for high-risk code changes.

use_cases.title: Security-Focused PR Triage
use_cases.description: A security engineer identifies secrets, injection risks, and vulnerable dependencies before merge.

use_cases.title: Release Readiness Review
use_cases.description: An engineering lead checks performance, tests, documentation, and merge readiness for a large feature pull request.

use_cases.title: Contributor Feedback
use_cases.description: An open source maintainer generates structured feedback and action items for external contributor pull requests.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review PR <number> in <owner/repo>. Focus on security, quality, tests, performance, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Risky Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review PR <number> in <owner/repo> with extra attention to authentication, authorization, secrets, and dependency changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare GitHub Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Review PR <number>, summarize merge readiness, and draft GitHub comments with prioritized action items.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Targeted Re-Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Re-review PR <number> after new commits. Compare changed files with earlier findings and update the merge readiness decision.

output_examples.input: Review PR 42 in acme/payments before merge.
output: Merge readiness: Changes Requested because authentication checks need fixes.
Security: one high issue and two medium issues require owner review.
Next actions: add tests for failed payment paths and update API documentation.

output_examples.input: Re-review PR 42 after new commits address security feedback.
output_examples.output: The new commits resolve the previous security finding. Remaining work is limited to documentation and one test coverage gap.

output_examples.input: Prepare feedback for a large refactor PR.
output: The report groups findings by security, performance, quality, tests, and documentation.
The merge decision stays pending until two complex functions are simplified and test coverage improves.

best_practices: Confirm repository and PR identifiers before running GitHub actions.
Run review agents in parallel, then synthesize one prioritized report.
Treat generated fixes as suggestions and verify them with tests.
anti_patterns: Posting automated approval without checking critical security findings.
Running referenced scripts from untrusted repositories without review.
Using the workflow when required GitHub or MCP credentials are unavailable.

faq.question: Does this skill post comments automatically?
faq.answer: It includes commands for posting comments, but execution depends on available GitHub tools and user permission.

faq.question: Does it include all referenced scripts?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package contains SKILL.md and a workflow diagram, so referenced scripts may be absent.

faq.question: Can it review large pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends batching large PRs by logical area and prioritizing high-risk files first.

faq.question: What agents does it coordinate?
faq.answer: It describes security, performance, code quality, test coverage, and documentation reviewers.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Should I trust the auto-fix suggestions?
faq.answer: Review suggestions manually and run tests before applying or merging generated changes.
